The Advanced Lab Manager manages the laboratories for two upper-division lab courses that comprise the Physics 111 Lab, enrolling 85-100 students per semester. This position plans, directs, executes and evaluates the operations of the lab on a day-to-day basis and participates in the committee of faculty and staff responsible for providing overall direction and establishing priorities for the 111 lab. The Advanced Lab Manager builds and maintains experiments, supports the management of a network of over 40 computers and servers, trains instructors in operation of the experiments, assists with student laboratory instruction, supervises student assistants, and purchases equipment and supplies. This position works with faculty, students, and staff to develop new experiments and performs engineering activities including conception, design, construction, and testing of experiments, as well as documentation and editing of instructional materials. The two courses managed by this position are critical to the success of the department's undergraduate major. It is in Physics 111 that students learn to do experimental physics, from experimental design, to hands-on experience in acquiring data and troubleshooting apparatus, to analyzing and communicating results in a professional manner. More than any other course, the 111 lab prepares students to work productively in an academic or industrial research environment.
Engineering support of upper-level physics instructional lab courses - 25%
Design, build and maintain functional laboratory stations for electronics and instrumentation course.
Assemble and maintain 20 or more complex experiments for advanced physics labs.
In collaboration with instructors, develop and maintain instructional materials, including lab manuals, additional readings, safety procedures, instructional videos, and course websites.
Estimate time, materials and labor costs for in-house machine shop fabrication.
Design and build research-grade instructional experiments, including magnetic field coils and power supplies for vacuum systems.
Generate design drawings and specifications for vacuum chambers, equipment racks, and optical benches for in-house machine shop fabrication.
Design circuits and feedback control systems for thermal electric controllers and cold traps.
Computer Programming and Technology - 25%

Support the management of the 111 lab information technology resources, including a server-based network of 40+ computers, and interface with an external systems administrator/security provider. Assign group policies to individual student accounts.
Write or oversee writing of programs for data acquisition, signal processing, and experiment control in LabView, Matlab, and other languages/applications as appropriate.

Design, update, and maintain the course Github and associated website. Provide online access by students and instructors to all instructional materials, including videos, published references, lab manuals, and software.
Produce, edit, and process to final form training videos for lab exercises and safety procedures.
Innovation and Development - 20%
Work with faculty, staff, and students to develop new experiments, overseeing all stages of development.
Determine project specifications and parameters.
Perform design, construction, assembly, and testing of complex experimental and instrument systems. Utilize departmental shops effectively in design and fabrication.
Write and edit instruction materials; pilot test new experiments with students.

Seek innovative ways to improve existing experiments, make experiments more costeffective and efficient, and enhance instructional opportunities. Consult experts outside the course instructors and university as appropriate.
Plan and administer lab schedules, schedules of due dates, and equipment assignments.
Assist with EH&S Safety inspections including Laser, Laboratory, and Radiation safety.
Maintain Chemical Inventory
Assign radiation rings to students and collect them by the end of the semester.
Create SOP's for experiments and the provide guidelines for safe use of lasers and radiation sources.
Maintain inventory of supplies and equipment to sustain operations without interruption; procure parts and equipment.

Plan and administer course budgets and other fund sources, such as grants and donations. Provide reports on financial status as needed to supervisor and 111 lab committee. Participate in grant-writing and fund-raising.
Promote a safe work environment for students, staff, and instructors. Comply with campuses, state, and federal requirements for safe conditions and procedures in the laboratory.
Serve on department or campus service committees as assigned.
Supervision and Instruction - 10%
Directly supervise 1-3 part-time student assistants (maximum 0.50 FTE) and any other staff positions that may be assigned. Schedule and assign projects.
Supervise summer student interns (typically two to four) working to develop and improve experiments.
Train and instruct faculty and graduate student instructors in the operation of experiments and in the ways that course policies are typically carried out.
Assist instructors with answering student questions and troubleshooting problems encountered by students during experiments.
Coordinate activities of six half-time graduate student instructors as directed by course faculty.
Ensure work is completed in a timely and efficient manner.
Employee Development - 5%
Attend workshops, conventions, and classes as needed to develop new programming and technical skills and knowledge.
Build relationships with colleagues doing some similar work at other universities through visits and participation in professional conferences.

Understanding of procedures within the Physics Department for requesting purchase orders, arranging for facilities maintenance and improvements, using departmental shops, and complying with requirements.
Expertise in Windows operating systems ranging from Windows 7 through the current OS. Familiarity with Windows Server, Unix, and Linux preferred.

Understanding of physical principles of classical physics, atomic physics, nuclear particle physics, lasers, solid state physics, optics, plasma physics, nonlinear dynamics, radioactive decay, astrophysics, biophysics, condensed matter, material sciences, and molecular physics.

Thorough knowledge associated with the planning, development, and construction of advanced physics experiments, specialized design work, and necessary to apply principles, practices and procedures in the completion of assignments.

Knowledge of campus environmental health and safety standards and procedures for general lab safety, hazardous waste handling and disposal, as well as for specialized requirements for radioactive sources and lasers.
Effective communication skills, both written and verbal, to convey complex information in a clear and concise manner.
Advanced interpersonal and presentation skills.
Ability to work in a collaborative manner; identify challenges and barriers and recommend resolutions, and ability to lead and influence others.
Information Technology knowledge sufficient to support the management of a large network of instructional computers.
Knowledge of campus business policies and procedures that affect the Lab.
Knowledge of electronics engineering, vacuum technology, electrical power, high voltage, digital logic circuits, analog circuits, cryogenics, and radiation and laser safety.
Skills to conduct electronics design, fabrication and repair, including soldering.
Working Knowledge of web technologies (Drupal, HTML, etc.), Adobe Suite, and Matlab.

Basic network knowledge (what is a MAC or IP address and how to find it), basic knowledge of Active Directory and Group Policy (domain accounts (CalNet IDs), AD Groups, what Group policy can do), and basic understanding of computer imaging.
Ability to produce training/educational videos.
